title: An Evaluation of Parental Question Characteristics and the Quality of AI Recommendations in Family Counseling for Children with Autism
content: A computational evaluation and prediction framework was developed to analyze how parental question characteristics affect the quality of generative AI recommendations in family counseling for children with autism. The framework integrates natural language preprocessing, structured feature encoding, semantic representation, quality calibration, machine-learning prediction, model interpretation, and cross-platform transfer validation. A total of 7,200 real counseling questions from 240 primary caregivers were paired with structured versions based on eight information fields, producing 14,400 question texts and 43,200 responses from three generative AI systems. Each question was represented by structured fields, a 768-dimensional semantic embedding, and an information-completeness measure. A multi-faceted Rasch model was used to calibrate expert ratings across six quality dimensions, and a multilevel ordered logit model quantified the effects of question characteristics. Logistic regression, Random Forest, LightGBM, and XGBoost were further compared for automated recommendation-quality prediction, while SHAP was used for feature interpretation and cross-platform validation was used to test model transferability. XGBoost achieved an AUC of 0.934, an F1 score of 0.879, and an accuracy of 0.892. Information completeness, behavioral-description accuracy, target clarity, and child-language clarity produced the largest SHAP contributions of 0.218, 0.176, 0.151, and 0.119, respectively. Cross-platform AUC ranged from 0.881 to 0.897. The results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating text feature engineering and machine-learning models into an automated quality-screening process for AI-assisted family counseling.
